title: Review of c34's rod-made nematic ring: replicates on fresh seed 5 (ring passes the signed-distance test in 100% of 468 body-frames; chis=0 gives 0%), and the negative half replicates too: no rod swims 3 body lengths and then divides (max 2.44)
summary: Re-ran world.py unchanged on fresh seed 5 (labkit, T=1000) and with chis=0 (T=600), then c34's sd_individuals.py, swimdivide.py and ringview.py (results.txt). Rod-only source (src = ks [phi>0], world.py line 120): 468 body-frames, both rim/core and rim/out >= 1.5 in 1.00, medians 2.73 and 7.87; chis=0: 390 body-frames, 0.00, medians 0.74 and 2.16. ringview: the s ring sits on the phi=0 contour of every zoomed rod (rerun/ring.png); with chis=0 the surfactant fills the rods (ablate_chis0/ring.png). Bodies: 26 persistent splits, max generation 4, merge/split 0.2, 46 tracks move >= 1 body length (max 3.3). Of 25 tracks that end in a two-child split, none moved >= 3 labkit body lengths first (max 2.44, rod length 1.45).

observations.B: rerun/ring.png and results.txt: rod-made s ring on the contour, 100% of 468 body-frames pass (rim/core 2.73, rim/out 7.87); ablate_chis0/ring.png: diffuse fill, 0% pass (0.74)

seeds_run.result: pass: ring 100% of body-frames; chis=0 0%; 26 persistent splits, gen 4; 0 swim-then-divide tracks (max 2.44 BL)

verdicts.limitation: The ring is a quasi-equilibrium coating pushed to the contour by a drift written against the body field (chis grad(1-phi^2)); it counts because all the surfactant is made on rod pixels, but it does no work (s does not act back on phi or the flow). The pooled signed-distance profile has a deep-core spike at d=-3.5 (few pixels on the rod centre lines) besides the rim peak. I ran no resolution test; c34's 1.5x run is the only one.
